accepted_history_scope.scope_judgment: Hermes correctly widened the sync target from recent AI Frontier/fast-channel work to the full 20260524 VectorFL/Hermes buildup arc.

accepted_structure_layers.meaning: No-call recovery, current-position proposal/apply history, reentry checks, compact handoff, and recovery/operator surface form the base evidence layer.
Scenario 1 and four-shape loop tests are the early functional rehearsal layer that made receipt/intake, space reading, merge, repeatability, and budget-gate behavior visible.
S1-S7 plus packet shape, source selection, guard priority, merge trace, role handoff, reentry/HOLD surface, and budget rollup are the tested internal VectorFL function layer.
Reviewed structure spec, bounded apply, intent correction, and relayering asset sample test turn Phase2 observations into structure and relayering proposals.
Hermes is the execution workbench; Codex retrieves and matures space; Gemini is only a Codex-side wide lens when ambiguity justifies it.
Provider-backed Codex/Gemini calls are not default execution paths; they require fresh-space or ambiguity justification and remain budget-governed.
AI Frontier EP93-EP97, infra-cost/context-economics, and fast-channel records are HOLD evidence and pattern/lens candidates, not authority.
Router, governance principle, dual-log namespace, quick exchange board, and skill candidate define the reusable Codex space-operator operating surface.

arc_level_space_delta.delta: The space began as recovery/current-position evidence with no-call and HOLD boundaries. Several early roots have UNKNOWN verdicts and should be treated as historical evidence until normalized by an authority/proposal status map.
Scenario and four-shape work supplied the behavioral substrate for later Phase2 function positions. This arc should not be discarded as miscellaneous; it is the prototype layer.
Phase2 converted prototype behavior into explicit tested functions: original preservation, source selection, guard priority, merge trace, role handoff, receipt/reentry surface, and budget rollup.
Phase3 moved from function validation into structure/relayering proposals. Its main value is the bounded-apply discipline and intent correction toward space relayering.
The loop matured from generic Codex/Gemini handoff into Hermes-centered execution: Hermes merges/executes; Codex operates space; Gemini is optional inside Codex-side exploration.
Invocation policy corrected the operational risk: direct provider calls are budget-governed exceptions, not the default path.
External AI Frontier materials added reusable lenses around operator load, context economics, infrastructure cost, and series-level pattern indexing.
Governance and channel work made the role split operational: namespace isolation, immutable cross-read artifacts, quick board, and skill packaging candidate.

gemini_exploration_decision.reason: The Hermes full-history packet has validated pointers, a chronological index, and enough arc structure for first-pass Codex judgment. Gemini is optional later only for cross-arc semantic flattening or layer ambiguity, not needed for this initial acceptance.
gemini_exploration_decision.optional_future_trigger: Use Gemini only if the full-history pattern index needs broad ambiguity review across foundation/Phase2/Phase3/Hermes-loop/AI-Frontier/channel layers.

maturation_proposals_hold_only.purpose: Separate historical evidence, approved current-position apply, and HOLD proposal records.

maturation_proposals_hold_only.purpose: This is enough for the commands 'check the space', 'analyze Hermes work', 'retrieve space for Hermes', and 'mature from reentry' without role collision.

maturation_proposals_hold_only.purpose: Make clear which older handoff artifacts are historical and which are superseded by Hermes-centered no-direct-API policy.

maturation_proposals_hold_only.purpose: Use it as external-space evidence for operator-load and context-economics, not as core authority.

maturation_proposals_hold_only.purpose: Ensure Gemini/Codex script-chain calls are traceable, bounded, and justified by ambiguity or fresh-space value.

missing_handles.reason: A compact index linking root seq, root path, sha256, arc, primary layer, current status, and supersession relation is not yet present as a Codex-owned artifact.
Older Codex/Gemini handoff/live-call artifacts need an explicit HOLD-only supersession map against the Hermes-centered policy.
Several foundation roots have UNKNOWN verdicts even though they are part of current-position history.
The system uses immutable versioned boards plus latest pointers, but a compact rule would prevent confusion between original quick board, rebuilt pointer board, and Codex-reviewed board.
A skill candidate exists, but installation/adoption as an active Codex skill remains separate from HOLD proposal work.

risks: Full-history scope can collapse back into recent-channel-only reading unless the arc index is preserved.
HOLD artifacts can be mistaken for authority if status fields are not normalized.
Older handoff files can conflict semantically with the newer Hermes-centered no-direct-API policy unless marked superseded.
Quick board pointer/hash versions can confuse readers if the latest-pointer rule is not explicit.
Provider-backed model calls can become default again unless context-economic justification is required.

stale_or_duplicate_handles_hold_only.reason: Root 001-006 are valid historical evidence but lack explicit verdicts in the full-history index.
Older direct handoff language should be kept as history but interpreted through the later Hermes-centered loop and invocation policy.
The scenario/four-shape items are structurally important and should not remain a catch-all bucket.
Validation records a prior pointer-order failure that was corrected; preserve as trace, not failure.
Later Codex and Gemini-assisted reviews exist; placeholders should be treated as waiting-state artifacts only.

summary: Codex accepts Hermes full-history sync as the correct current reading frame. The space should now be matured around full-history arc indexing, status normalization, supersession mapping, and Codex space-operator skill/channel consolidation, all HOLD-only.
